title: Cross-Regional Grapevine Cold Hardiness Prediction via Learned Multimodal Latent Representations
abstract: arXiv:2608.31097v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Accurate daily predictions of cold hardiness in woody plants are critical in regions where freezing temperatures can damage dormant buds and reduce seasonal yield. Existing biophysical, hybrid, and deep learning models have shown high predictive accuracy when trained on local data but remain largely site-specific. The limited availability of cold hardiness data, coupled with the lack of principled methods for transferring cold hardiness predictions to new regions and cultivars, has limited the broader adoption and practical utility of these approaches, particularly in data-scarce regions. To address these limitations, we propose a cold hardiness prediction framework that learns a transferable latent representation by capturing region-specific variation through learned embeddings. To enable prediction in previously unseen regions, we infer embeddings from (1) text descriptions of the cultivar and growing region, and (2) limited historical

translated_title: 基于学习型多模态潜在表示的跨区域葡萄抗寒性预测
translated_abstract: 在低温可能损害休眠芽并降低季节产量的地区，对木本植物抗寒性进行准确的日常预测至关重要。现有的生物物理模型、混合模型和深度学习模型在本地数据上训练时表现出较高的预测精度，但在很大程度上仍然局限于特定地点。抗寒性数据的有限可用性，加上缺乏将抗寒性预测迁移到新区域和新品种的原则性方法，限制了这些方法的更广泛采用和实际效用，尤其是在数据稀缺的地区。为了解决这些局限性，我们提出了一种抗寒性预测框架，该框架通过学习嵌入来捕捉区域特异性变化，从而学习可迁移的潜在表示。为了在以前未见过的区域实现预测，我们从（1）品种和种植区域的文本描述，以及（2）有限的历史数据中推断嵌入。
tldr: 提出了一种通过学习可迁移的多模态潜在表示来进行跨区域葡萄抗寒性预测的框架，利用品种和种植区域的文本描述及有限历史数据，使模型能够推广到数据稀缺的未见地区。
en_tdlr: A cold hardiness prediction framework that learns transferable latent representations via learned embeddings, enabling cross-regional grapevine cold hardiness predictions in unseen, data-scarce regions using cultivar/region text descriptions and limited historical data.
